::: {.letter-metadata}
**Date:** Decr 8th 1865  
**From:** Elderfield, Otterbourne, Winchester.  
**Manuscript:** British Library Add MSS 54920: 121-2
:::

Dear [Mr Macmillan](people/person_939.qmd)
I have written a new preface and sent it to [Spottiswood](organizations/other_183.qmd). If I did not send the former one to you I wonder what I did with it, I suppose it will come out of some strange corner.[^1]

I am glad you and [Mrs Daniel](people/person_941.qmd) think well of the [Chaplet](cmy_books/cmybook_69.qmd). I only wish I could give my French ladies more French grace. I have about four chapters more written but not re written, and I doubt being able to finish it quickly without spoiling it, but I will go on in earnest with it now.

I thought there was so much a set against historical romance just now that it was hardly safe to send it forth on its own legs & without feeling its way. However the [Dove](cmy_books/cmybook_62.qmd) may be a pioneer, only would not publishing this in the spring be following rather too close upon her heels? I was much interested in the [article](other_books/otherbook_436.qmd) on [Mrs Gaskell](people/person_1965.qmd), but I do not agree to the acute feelings of authoresses as to criticism - and I have known some pretty sharp critiques on others besides myself - that have not done much harm to their feelings. I was struck too by the hoar frost description in [Craddock Nowell](other_books/otherbook_399.qmd), or rather the break up of the hoar frost, it is so exactly what I have often watched.

We are in much trouble for [my brothe](people/person_1624.qmd)r’s [youngest](people/person_1592.qmd), a little girl of 16 months is in what I fear is a most hopeless state from whooping cough and teething convulsions though so strong a child that there have been two terrible days of lingering

Yours sincerely
C M Yonge

---

[^1]: This was the preface to *The Prince and the Page*.
